title: The SDE level rubric: does it need more than one person to be true; must it be coordinated; is it about the whole and how it receives or projects information; and the horizon rubric: immediate (discrete action), medium (process), long (experiment) (2026-11-07)

sections.name: narrative
sections.label: Narrative
sections.content:
So, the inability to place a level is interesting.

My perception here has been trained by tarot and zodiac.

Fo sde, the rules on the surface were:

Does this need more than one person to be true? Does this define something that can be known, done , owned, felt.

Is this something that must be coordinated? Is this something a group needs to know to act together?

Is this about the whole and how it receives or projects information?

Another rubric was related to the horizon. Level 1 tends to be immediate. It's a property of the moment. It changes discreet action.

Level 2 is medium term. It requires establishing and modifying process.

Level 3 is long term. It requires experiment and exploration

sections.label: Source
sections.content: The owner, in conversation with Claude Code, 2026-11-07, answering the finding that no model of any size reads the SDE level axis (component/relationships/system, kappa 0.00 to 0.09) from the agent's definitions; recorded verbatim. The three questions map to levels 1 to 3 (component, relationships, system); the horizon rubric is a second reading of the same axis.
